use: The standard contract has no home warranty clause. Buyer and seller can add one with a separate addendum.

struck: So a long-time owner's bill, and the tax credit at closing, is usually smaller than one figured on the price.
use: When a home's last deed is old, its tax bill, and the tax credit at closing, is often smaller than one figured on today's price.

struck: Once asked, the loan servicer must send an accurate payoff statement within seven business days.
use: On a home loan made for personal use, the servicer must send an accurate payoff statement within seven business days of a written request. A loan made to buy a rental the owner does not use counts as a business loan, and that rule does not cover it. A beach place the owner planned to use more than 14 days a year still counts as personal.

struck: South Carolina bars a transfer fee recorded after February 2012 that sends money to a third party on each sale.
use: South Carolina bars a transfer fee covenant recorded after February 1, 2012 that makes an owner pay a third party on each sale.

struck: About 6 in 10 Horry County condo owners, and about 1 in 5 house owners, get their tax bill at an address outside South Carolina.
use: About 6 in 10 Horry County condo units, and about 1 in 5 other homes, have their tax bill mailed to an address outside South Carolina.

struck: In a standard South Carolina closing, the buyer's attorney usually prepares the settlement statement and pays off the seller's mortgage from the sale.
use: In a standard South Carolina closing, the buyer's attorney typically prepares the settlement statement. When that attorney also sends the seller's mortgage payoff, the attorney may add a reasonable payoff handling fee to the seller's side, though the seller is not the attorney's client. A seller may refuse to sign a settlement statement they do not agree with.
